name: Milan
tagline: Marble spires, Leonardo and modern Italian life
summary: Use Milan as a practical northern-Italy gateway with strong art, design and railway connections. Put the Duomo, Galleria and historic centre together; reserve Leonardo’s Last Supper separately, then explore Brera, the castle or Navigli.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are comfortable for city walking. Summer can be hot, winter foggy, and major fairs can raise hotel prices.
arrival: Malpensa has rail connections to central Milan; Linate connects by metro. Bergamo arrivals require a longer bus or rail transfer. Verify the airport before choosing accommodation.
gettingAround: Metro, trams and walking cover the central sights. Group the Duomo area, Brera/castle and Leonardo/Sant’Ambrogio into separate walks.
cashTip: Carry a modest amount of local cash for small purchases; use cards where accepted and check menu or ticket prices before paying.
foodTip: Try risotto alla milanese and panzerotti, with dedicated vegetarian and menu-labelled halal alternatives available.
buyTip: Browse design objects, stationery and fashion; window-shopping is free even in the luxury district.
baseArea: Brera or the historic centre for walking; Centrale for onward trains; Porta Venezia for dining and transit.
